summary: Tested AYMAFIN backend (18 pytest tests, 17 pass) and frontend E2E (landing -> register -> 4-step onboarding -> dashboard -> forecasting -> reports -> chat). Backend: auth (register/login/me/logout), business CRUD, analysis, forecasts, reports + real PDF download (>1KB, %PDF header), chat (mock replies + history) all WORKING. Frontend: all data-testids reachable, lang switcher AR -> dir=rtl OK, full happy-path flow works. ONE CRITICAL backend security finding: brute-force lockout (5-fail -> 429) is NOT enforced in the preview environment (returned 401 then 200 on correct password even after 7 wrong attempts).

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout never returns 429. After 5+ wrong-password attempts on the same email, the next correct-password attempt returns 200 instead of 429. Likely root cause: identifier is built as f'{request.client.host}:{email}' but behind the K8s ingress, request.client.host is the in-cluster proxy/pod IP and may vary across requests, so login_attempts records are never aggregated to 5. Recommend keying on email only (or X-Forwarded-For) and ALSO rejecting login while locked_until>now even on correct password — the current check works in theory but is bypassed because attempts never reach threshold.

minor.issue: When threshold trips, code resets attempts=0 and only stores locked_until. After locked_until expires, an attacker gets a fresh 5-attempt window. Consider keeping an audit counter.
Auth cookie set with secure=False even though preview runs on HTTPS. Browsers accept it for now (samesite=lax) but secure=True would be safer in production.

issues: Default UI language renders as EN even though i18n.js is documented to default to FR — likely picks browser language or persisted choice; verify intended default.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout: change identifier to email-only (or use X-Forwarded-For for IP behind ingress). Verify by repeating 5 wrong-password attempts via curl — 6th should return 429.
Set secure=True on auth cookie in production (preview uses HTTPS).
(Optional) Confirm intended default language on landing — currently EN; if FR is intended, force i18n init lng to 'fr' regardless of browser.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: brute-force identifier 'ip:email' is unreliable behind a proxy — switch to email-only or honour X-Forwarded-For.
server.py: in lockout branch, attempts is reset to 0 — a determined attacker can keep cycling 5-attempt windows; consider locking the user record instead.
server.py uses @app.on_event('startup')/'shutdown') which are deprecated in FastAPI; migrate to lifespan handlers.
compute_analysis recommendations are hard-coded French strings — won't be translated when UI is in EN/AR. Either return i18n keys or localise on the frontend.
Cookie secure=False on HTTPS preview is OK for dev but must be True in prod.

rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force lockout bug RCA — Reproduction: register a fresh user, send 5+ wrong-password POST /api/auth/login, then send a correct password — should return 429 but returns 200. Root cause hypothesis: identifier `f'{request.client.host}:{email}' ` resolves request.client.host to the in-cluster ingress proxy IP that varies between requests (or to a pod-internal address), so each failed attempt creates/updates a different document and attempts never reach LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD=5. Fix: derive client IP from `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or request.client.host`, or simply key by email only for lockout. Also consider not resetting attempts to 0 when locking, and reject correct-password logins while locked_until is in the future (current code already does this — the bug is solely that attempts never accumulate).
